query: Footwork Until Dark Lyra finds you after practice. "The captain's notes say the stance is everything," she says. "Your stance is a disgrace. Three hours. Now." She has already chalked the marks on the floor. Drill until dark She is merciless and exact. By dark you can set your feet without thinking, and you never want to see a chalk mark again. "Better," she says, which from Lyra is a sonnet. "Tomorrow. I have an essay." She looks at you as if you'd chosen to lose. You write the essay. It is a fine essay, and Lyra mentions your stance at breakfast.
